title: Questions about new bullet in `eligible for autoplay`
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

In @scottjehl's recent commit 489e0b6d, the [eligible for autoplay](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#eligible-for-autoplay) algorithm got a new bullet point:
> if it is an `audio` or `video` element and its lazy loading attribute is either in the Eager state or has started loading while in the Lazy state, or scripting is disabled for the element;

This puzzled me in various ways.
- The structure is "if X and Y, or Z;", and it isn't obvious to me whether I should be grouping "(X and Y)" vs "(Y, or Z)".

- At first I thought the initial "if" was just a typo -- it doesn't appear in any other condition in the list, or (I believe) in *any* such "when all of the following are true" list. But then it occurred to me that the "if" is there to indicate that the bulk of this bullet only needs to be true under a particular guard condition. If that's the case, then presumably the guard isn't `X and Y`, because `if GUARD, or Z;` is just weird. So then the guard must be just X (i.e., `it is an audio or video element`), and the structure is `if GUARD and (Y or Z)`. (This would be clearer with "then" instead of "and": `if GUARD then Y or Z`.)

- `Y` is `its lazy loading attribute is either in the Eager state or has started loading while in the Lazy state`. Expanding the elision, this is equivalent to `either its lazy loading attribute is in the Eager state or its lazy loading attribute has started loading while in the Lazy state`. But I think it might be a category error to ask whether an attribute has started loading.

- In trying to determine what *can* be said to have started loading, I note that the phrase "has started loading" is not linked, and there is no other occurrence of "has started loading" (or even just "started loading") in the spec. Searching for "loading" finds 313 hits, which would be a lot to slog through. It feels like there should be a link for this.

@zcorpan has addressed some of these points in Matrix, but asked me to file an issue.
